## Headline: Madras High Court Grills Tamil Nadu Government Over Scrapping Parandur Airport While Supreme Court Intervenes in Madurai Deepam Dispute

## The Big Picture
Tamil Nadu's political landscape is experiencing intense friction across judicial, administrative, and legislative domains, centered on policy reversals, resource allocation disputes, and religious observances. The Madras High Court's sharp scrutiny of the state administration regarding the cancellation of the Parandur greenfield airport project—which had already incurred expenditures totaling Rs 680 crore—has created immediate legal vulnerabilities for the ruling government. Concurrently, inter-state tensions over water rights reached a climax as the Supreme Court dismissed the state government's petitions seeking additional Cauvery water releases from Karnataka, prompting fierce opposition leaders like DMK president M.K. Stalin to demand an all-party assembly and direct appeals to Union leadership.

Adding to the administrative turmoil, high-profile corruption probes, including Central Crime Branch raids on former DMK Minister P. Moorthi over alleged illegal gravel quarrying causing a Rs 5.39 crore state exchequer loss, have galvanized political posturing across opposition ranks. Meanwhile, the legal tussle over the Thirupparankundram Deepam row escalated to the Supreme Court, which permitted a restricted, one-time Karthigai Deepam lighting at Madurai's 'Deepathoon' while barring public entry to maintain civil order. These multi-faceted developments underscore a volatile governance environment where administrative accountability, judicial interventions, and competitive regional politics dictate the state's immediate trajectory.

## Top Political Developments
### 1. Madras High Court Questions State Government on Abandoning Parandur Airport After Rs 680 Crore Outlay
- **Verification Status:** Multi-Source Verified
The Madras High Court came down heavily on the Tamil Nadu government during a PIL hearing challenging the administration's abrupt decision to scrap the proposed Parandur Greenfield Airport project. A division bench questioned the rationale behind dropping a strategically vital infrastructure initiative after public funds amounting to Rs 680 crore had already been expended on land acquisition and preliminary preparatory works. Petitioners and legal counsels argued that abandoning the project without cogent economic justification results in substantial financial loss to the state exchequer and derails regional industrial expansion. ### 2. Supreme Court Permits One-Time Karthigai Deepam Lighting at Madurai Deepathoon, Restricting Public Access
- **Verification Status:** Multi-Source Verified
In a decisive intervention addressing escalating communal and political tensions in southern Tamil Nadu, the Supreme Court permitted a restricted, one-time Karthigai Deepam lighting ceremony at the disputed 'Deepathoon' site on Madurai hill for November 24. Acknowledging security concerns raised by local authorities and competing petitions, the apex court bench explicitly barred public entry to the immediate monument zone while staying the earlier contradictory directions issued by the Madras High Court. ## Government and Administration
- **Central Crime Branch Raids Former DMK Minister P. Moorthi in Rs 5.39-Crore Illegal Gravel Quarrying Case:** The Central Crime Branch (CCB) and district police executed coordinated early morning raids on Friday at the Madurai and Sivaganga residences of former DMK Minister for Registration P. Moorthi, alongside properties owned by his relatives. The high-profile crackdown stems from two registered cases by the Madurai District Crime Branch alleging that Moorthi, his son, and relatives Rajamani, Anantha Kumar, and Senthil Kumar extracted gravel and minerals far beyond permitted lease limits from agricultural and barren lands, resulting in an estimated revenue loss of Rs 5.39 crore to the state exchequer. Operating under Deputy Superintendent of Police supervision, search teams scoured premises across Iyer Bungalow, Poovanthi, Alanganallur, and Vadipatti to seize financial records and digital devices. Addressing the media, former Minister Moorthi vehemently denied all allegations of illegal excavation, claiming he had merely leased out his private land for standard quarrying operations and possessed no knowledge of any over-extraction or regulatory violations. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/police-search-former-dmk-minister-moorthys-residence-in-rs-539-crore-quarry-irregularities-case))

## Political Parties and Opposition
- **M.K. Stalin Demands All-Party Meet on Cauvery Crisis as Supreme Court Rejects State Pleas:** DMK president M.K. Stalin launched a sharp verbal assault on Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on Friday, asserting that 'the ego of the Chief Minister is not bigger than the tears of farmers' as he reiterated demands for an immediate all-party meeting. Stalin's remarks came in the wake of the Supreme Court's dismissal of Tamil Nadu government petitions seeking mandatory additional water releases from Karnataka to rescue the state's samba crops. Insisting that partisan posturing must cease, Stalin urged the Chief Minister to unite all political stakeholders before leading a high-powered delegation to New Delhi to press Prime Minister Narendra Modi for immediate intervention under the Cauvery Water Management Authority framework. Echoing the sentiment for cross-party unity, Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president B. Manickam Tagore also called for political solidarity to block Karnataka's controversial Mekedatu dam proposal, urging regional parties to halt mutual recriminations and defend state agrarian rights collectively. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/convene-all-party-meet-on-cauvery-cms-ego-not-bigger-than-farmers-tears-mk-stalin))

## Assembly, Courts, and Policy
- **Madras High Court Restrains Circulation of Junior Vikatan Illustration Targeting Former DMK Minister E.V. Velu:** In an order protecting political figures from defamatory media depictions, the Madras High Court granted an interim injunction restraining the further publication, circulation, or digital dissemination of a controversial caricature published by Tamil bi-weekly magazine *Junior Vikatan*. The illustration targeted former DMK Minister E.V. Velu, prompting senior legal counsel to move the court on grounds of severe reputational damage and malicious targeting designed to influence public opinion amidst ongoing political investigations. The bench reviewed the submitted digital clippings and editorial content before issuing the interim restraint, directing the publication's management and associated social media platforms to remove existing posts carrying the disputed artwork pending further hearings. Legal analysts noted that the ruling reinforces strict boundaries regarding journalistic commentary on active political personalities, balancing freedom of the press with individual defamation protections under civil law. ([The Hindu](https://www.thehindu.com))

## District-Level Developments
- **Tragic Electrocution of Mourner in Tiruttani Triggers Outrage Over Municipal Equipment Safety:** A 65-year-old woman, Devaki of Kasinathapuram village, was tragically electrocuted on Wednesday while paying her final respects to a deceased neighbor in Nehru Nagar, Tiruttani taluk, Tiruvallur district. The victim touched a municipal freezer box borrowed from the Tiruttani Municipality to preserve the body, which suffered a severe internal electrical short circuit. Thirteen other mourners attempting to rescue her also sustained non-fatal electric shocks before power was manually disconnected. Left parties and local civic groups strongly condemned municipal authorities for releasing malfunctioning, uncertified electrical equipment to grieving families without safety checks, demanding immediate compensation of Rs 10 lakh for the victim's kin and criminal negligence proceedings against the municipal commissioner and maintenance contractors. Tiruvallur district administration officials announced a formal inquiry into municipal equipment procurement protocols and promised stricter safety audits for all civic-leased utility items. ([DT Next](https://www.dtnext.in/news/tamilnadu/woman-mourner-at-funeral-electrocuted-by-faulty-freezer-box-supplied-tiruttani-municipality))

## What to Watch Next
Over the next 24 to 48 hours, political observers will closely monitor the execution of the Supreme Court's restricted Karthigai Deepam lighting order at Madurai's 'Deepathoon' on November 24 to gauge law enforcement efficacy and compliance by local factions. Additionally, attention will shift to the Madras High Court's impending proceedings regarding the Parandur airport cancellation report and the potential fallout from the Central Crime Branch raids on former Minister P. Moorthi. Opposition parties are expected to finalize protest dates regarding the Cauvery water dispute following M.K. Stalin's renewed push for an all-party delegation.
